newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dresdner board member says euro will weaken unions.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner board member says euro will weaken unions.

text.p: Ernst-Moritz Lipp of Germany's Dresdner Bank AG predicted on Wednesday that the transition to a single European currency would end trade union wage talks at the European level, substantially weakening unions' power.

Speaking to reporters at a Paris seminar on the euro, Lipp, who is a Dresdner board member and an economics professor, also predicted the shift to the euro would increase wage disparities across Europe and even within nations.
Dresdner is Germany's second largest commercial bank.
If there were one wage level across Europe, companies would quickly migrate to high-productivity regions, leaving low-productivity regions bereft of jobs, he said.

"So it is the low-productivity regions that would refuse Europe-wide negotiations," he said. "The tendency today is already away from nationwide wage negotiations and towards wage negotiations at the company level."

Lipp said it was "impossible to set wages on a European-wide level because the economic conditions are so different from place to place. There is no justification to accept Europe-wide talks. It would destroy hundreds of thousands of workplaces."
Earlier in the seminar, Lipp predicted the euro would "practically eliminate" trade unions in Europe.

But after being reminded by a fellow banker that journalists were attending the seminar, he said he meant only that unions would be reduced to an advisory capacity in salary talks which would in future take place primarily at the company level.
